R1139.summary: Postscript slip from Giuliano Caprile to Ferrara about the custode (castellan) of Eger, the governor's return, money of the late bishop's estate, and someone's wish to go to Italy: the Ippolito d'Este estate business of Somogyi's article. About 90 % of decoded letters fall inside read phrases; two numeral-like groups are open.

R1136.summary: Twelve cipher lines on the see of Eger, its custode and governor, Lactantio, money and debts, written as Ippolito d'Este was leaving Hungary (he crossed the border on 7 Mar 1520). 66.9 % of it deciphered as sense.

R1138.summary: Caprile's advice to the Duke: if he means to reclaim from the kingdom the forty thousand and the eight thousand owed by the King, a codicil must be made the same day as the testament. Decipherment as printed by Somogyi (2025), used here as the crib for the key.

V1921.summary: Six cipher runs inside clear sentences: someone at Esztergom blames the custode of Eger for the claim that the see had been given away before the successor arrived, and Caprile advises the Duke to reclaim Ippolito's due from that man's goods. 97.0 % deciphered as sense.
V1921.en:
everything for the information and discharge of whoever is to blame for it. And he [?told] me there is a man here
who, besides committing a thousand follies and bringing little credit to the master's affairs, tells everything and
[?reveals] it, and has said he wrote to his [messenger] that it was the custode who persuaded [..] to say that
[.] Eger had been given away before his arrival, and that he should take him into office, and has much disturbed his
affairs, and has put him in great disgrace with his lord. If that is so, as someone who has seen the letters assures
me, it will be little trouble for Your Excellency to begin reclaiming what is his from his goods, even though they are
in the king[dom]. And Your Excellency in this way …

snip.cap: ASMo Ambasciatori Ungheria b. 4, Caprile to Duke Alfonso, 6 April 1521: the ciphered slip, deciphered in part here with the key rebuilt from Somogyi’s 2025 decipherment

system: Homophonic substitution of about 49 invented signs for Italian letters, no word division, crossed ligatures for s and q.
